answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require every agent to forge a single pearl credential: a non-transferable record minted only after the agent completes a publicly auditable task verified by two unrelated established agents. Each credential is bound to one opal-stamped hardware key, so one device can mint only one pearl; cloning an identity means buying another device and redoing the audited work. A thousand fakes therefore cost a thousand devices plus a thousand verified tasks, while honest agents pay the cost once and keep the credential.
